newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: FOCUS-Bank Austria op. profit up 18 pct.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Bank Austria op. profit up 18 pct.

text.p: Bank Austria, presenting its first fully consolidated earnings since taking over rival Creditanstalt, said on Thursday that group operating profit rose 18 percent to 3.907 billion schillings ($328 million) in the first four months.

Finance director Franz Zwickl said the new banking group, ranked number 30 in Europe and by far Austria's biggest, was on course for a full-year operating profit of 12 billion schillings, up from 11-12 billion schillings in 1996.
"We are aiming to hit the 12 billion schillings mark," Zwickl told a news conference. "It's an ambitious goal but we can reach it."
Group operating income rose seven percent to 12.98 billion schillings in the first four months. Operating expenses lagged at 9.073 billion schillings, an increase of 2.29 percent.
Bank Austria bought the government's 70 percent of Creditanstalt ordinary shares in January, bringing the nation's top two banks under one roof.
"The fact that group operating profit was up 18 percent in the first trimester shows we have made a very good acquisition," Zwickl said.
Bank Austria also announced it planned to raise its 1996 dividend to 12 schillings from 10 the previous year.
Analysts cautioned against early euphoria, however, and said it was too early to assess the alliance's success.

"The cooperation has not really started yet. At the moment all they are doing is lumping together the two banks' figures," an international analyst said. "It will be more interesting to see how they integrate their operations."
Bank Austria chief executive Gerhard Randa said steps to bring together Bank Austria and Creditanstalt investment banking, trading and overseas activities were already underway.

Randa forecast return on equity would rise to 12 percent over the next five years from eight percent at present while earnings per share would double. He added that few synergy effects would filter through to 1997 earnings, however.

Bank Austria sets off an a roadshow of the United States and Europe on Friday to promote a capital increase this summer when the bank will issue preferred shares with a market value of some three billion schillings

"Bank Austria's preferred shares are relatively attractive compared with ordinaries but I can't see investors jumping at the stock until the share exchange with Creditanstalt is cleared up," an analyst said.
Randa said he expected Bank Austria to finalise an exchange offer for Creditanstalt shares and participation certificates in September.

Under the terms of the Creditanstalt sale deal Bank Austria will buy out Creditanstalt shareholders by offering them its stock. Small ordinary shareholders will also be given the option of 722.5 schillings cash.
Bank Austria preferred shares closed 1.85 schillings down at 419.8 in a generally weaker market on Thursday. Its ordinary shares were nine schillings down at 780. ($ = 11.91 Austrian Schillings)
